Chapter 6. The Weight of a Name.
There’s something almost mysterious about names, isn’t there? The way they can hold so much, and sometimes, hide even more.
For years, she lived behind the shield of “Emily Doe.” It was a name that kept her safe, but also kept her a step removed from her own life.
Imagine watching your own words travel the world—your victim impact statement read by millions—while you remain just a shadow, a symbol, never quite real to the people who most needed to see you.
In the quiet of her apartment, she’d sometimes pull up that statement, reading it over again. She could still feel the trembling in her hands as she typed, and the way her heart thudded when she finally read it aloud in court.
At first, she never expected her words to leave the courtroom. But they did.
Strangers started reaching out—sharing their own stories, thanking her for saying what they couldn’t. And she felt it—the weight of their hope, their pain, and their gratitude, all piled on her shoulders.
But anonymity, as comforting as it can be, is also a double-edged sword. She could walk down the street and blend in, but at the same time, she felt invisible—as if her true self was slowly disappearing. Even at family gatherings, she was still a daughter, a sister, but there was always part of her that stayed hidden, even from the people she loved most.
That longing grew—the urge to step out from behind the mask, to finally claim her story as her own.
Deciding to reveal her name wasn’t easy. She thought about everything she’d be giving up—her privacy, the quiet, the safety. She worried about backlash, about being forever marked by what had happened. But she also wondered: what if there was freedom in owning her story? What if she could finally be seen as a whole person, not just a victim?
Most people don’t realize just how much courage it takes to step forward like that.
She weighed all her options, talked it through with her family, and really listened to her own heart. In the end, she made the choice to reclaim her name.
She became Chanel Miller—a person with a past, a present, and a future.
The first time she saw her real name in print, the feeling was electric—a mix of exhilaration and fear. She was no longer just a symbol. She was real, with a voice, a face, and a story that was truly hers.
The world responded with incredible support, but also with the kind of scrutiny that comes with being truly seen. Chanel braced herself for whatever might come, but deep down, she felt a new kind of strength.
She wasn’t hiding anymore. She was finally, fully herself.
